Now, you said that you were familiar with Warsaw Pact countries and also, by extension, some of the JNA activities. Do you recognise this target coordinate system that the -- was used by the HV?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a similar target system that we use in our army. It can be based upon another kind of mapping but it says just a grids where a target it and the heights of a target. So it is very obvious what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in this vein, sir, that in order to know exactly what you're talking about, obviously you have to take the grids and plot it out? I'm talking about the hospital to begin with those grid coordinates of 79300, 95530 and 230?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when you want to use any information that is on a map the first thing to do is it, of course, you start using those -- those information, those target coordinates and plot them on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did that together with the OTP. They presented me that list and I have not been checking all the grid because I take the information as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No. My question is: Did you actually take these grid coordinates for the hospital and plot them on the map using the X/Y grid coordinates?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me bring up, to begin with, 1D65-0495. As this is coming up, you would agree with me the obvious solution to this is to be sure exactly what you are firing upon you need to plot out the grids, don't you?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now what we have dont in this case, Mr. President, is take a map that has been received in evidence, D131, with any number of targets. And we have taken the grid coordinates for each of these items, as you can see 710 which is in quotes, a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, I think there's a problem with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it a similar problem as we had yesterday? I do understand that it has been fixed, Mr. Kehoe. Another reminder that not only human beings but even technical equipment may suffer from our speed of speech. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think my last question is missing from the transcript, and if I can just re-ask that question again, Mr. President because I don't think it made it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course, you can put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I know this is repeating the question, Colonel, but it didn't make it to the transcripts. My question was in order to be sure of the particular location that is being fired upon, you have to go to the grid coordinates and actually map it out, that's the way you do it, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, looking at this map, and we know from KV 10. If I can just explain, Mr. President, what was done here that likewise didn't make it to the transcript before we move actually to KV10 -- excuse me KV 710, apologies. We have taken a document that is previously received in evidence, D131. Within D131, we have overlaid the grid coordinates for the KV -- the target list, the KV numbers as presented in P1271. Now, looking at KV 710, sir, the one that -- you see that location that is up at the top part of that page?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now in this item, A 4 which is right next to it. A 4 has been testified to as a RSK unit base mortars that was near this high school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could go three items -- three maps up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, what we have here, sir, is an area that was identified by a witness as a mortar location. The grid coordinates for 710 and the hospital which is off to the right. Now, as can you see, sir, that even though this is some writing calling this the hospital, the grid coordinates place it in a field next to an ARSK mortar battery. Are you with me on this, sir?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And under the circumstances with a military position in that location, that is certainly -- excuse me, that is certainly a proper place for artillery to fire; Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I do not -- the ARSK mortar unit deployment which is apparently in the red dot where the arrow is pointing, I don't see then that is in itself a logic military target to be fired upon. Although, I made my remarks upon firing upon a single mortar unit. But that's one thing. But the target titled hospital somewhere in the middle of a forest apparently has no military value to me in this thing all. But I cannot understand then for that reason why it occurs in a target list mentioning the name hospital, because that is something that is absolutely impossible for me to read in a target list that you have the name hospital there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It looks like someone inaccurately described that area, isn't it? And that's why you rely on the grid coordinates, right? Ht.

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Because the grid coordinates are the single most important thing in targeting right.

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grid coordinates are very important, absolutely true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me a second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And with regard to actual mortar position, sir I think you said - and I don't have the actual reference - but correct me if I'm wrong, mortar positions are positions that can move, right? People pick their mortars and go to another location; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the only thing I said about the mortar position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. That's just one of them?

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but it is important to remember all of the things that I said, because, first of all, they can move very quickly; and, secondly, it's only one small mortar unit that has no military value in the whole operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. Let's go back to P1271.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I just noticed that we're almost completed, Your Honour. I don't know if you want me to go into this line of inquiry on this particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know how much time you think it will take, but if it would be more than two or three minute, I would rather adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It would be more than two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kehoe, but I'm also addressing the other Defence teams, are your estimates as far as the time needed for the cross-examination of Mr. Konings still valid? I see Mr. Cayley nodding yes. That is zero. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes, they are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Konings, might not come as a surprise that I give you the same instructions that I did before, that is, not to speak with anyone about your testimony. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume on Monday, the 19th of January, 9.00 in the morning, in this same Courtroom I; and I would like to especially thank transcribers and interpreters and wish them full recovery over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
